chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, who said:

I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) working in his land, his feet having become soaked in sweat. I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, where are the men (workers)?' He said, 'O Ali! Those who worked by their hands in their land and in my father's land, who are better than me.' I said to him, 'Who are they?' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Commander of the Faithful, and my forefathers (peace be upon them), all of them had worked by their hands. And this is from the work of the Prophets, the Messengers, the Successors, and the Righteous.'
ai.seo_question: Did the Shia Imams engage in manual labor and work with their own hands?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the Shia principle of *ittiba’* (emulation) by highlighting the Imam’s personal engagement in manual labor, specifically agriculture, to validate the dignity of worldly livelihood. It establishes a continuous chain of practice from the Prophet and Imam Ali through the Imams, framing manual work not merely as necessity but as an act of worship and a distinctive trait of the *Awsiya’* (successors) and righteous servants.
